candidates.summary: the cap drops directly changed realms, while the comment it feeds still links every one of them and says they are always kept
candidates.failure_scenario: A sweep pull request that edits more than -max-realms realms directly (a tree-wide `gno = "0.9"` bump touches every gnomod.toml, and renderRelevant treats gnomod.toml as render-relevant; examples/gno.land/r holds 58 realm packages against a default cap of 25) leaves ChangedRealms longer than Realms. comment.go:62 links every ChangedRealms entry and comment.go:86 prints "the changed realms are always kept", so the posted PR comment offers 33 preview links that 404 on the published snapshot and tells the reviewer nothing was dropped. Run with 3 changed realms and maxRealms=1: Realms=[gno.land/r/x/a], the comment links r/x/b and r/x/c anyway.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b7-claims-cap-bounds_test.go misc/gnopreview/zz_b7_claims_test.go && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestB7CapDropsChangedRealms -v ./...
candidates.evidence: ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/x/a gno.land/r/x/b gno.land/r/x/c] Realms=[gno.land/r/x/a] Dropped=2; "changed realm gno.land/r/x/b   rendered=false linked in comment=true"; "comment asserts the changed realms are always kept while 2 of them were dropped". find examples/gno.land/r -name gnomod.toml | wc -l = 58.

low_band.summary: the gnoweb seed realms are appended after the cap, so Realms can hold maxRealms+4
low_band.failure_scenario: plan.go:71 says Realms is "capped at MaxRealms", plan.go:192 says "maxRealms caps how many realms are rendered" and the README says "At most 25 realms are rendered". The four gnowebSeedRealms are appended after the truncation, so a PR that touches gnoweb and 25+ realms boots gnodev on 29 packages and crawls them. Measured with maxRealms=1: len(Realms)=5.

low_band.summary: Empty reports a gnoweb-only plan with no realms as worth previewing, and render then indexes Realms[0]
low_band.failure_scenario: Empty is !Gnoweb && len(Realms)==0, so a gnoweb-only change whose four seed realms are all absent from the tree (a rename or a move of gnoland/home, docs/security_patterns, gnoland/boards2/v0 and gnoland/blog) returns Empty()==false with Realms empty. main.go:131 then evaluates urlOf(plan.Realms[0]) and the render job panics with index out of range instead of printing "nothing to preview". plan_test.go's "gnoweb alone" case pins exactly that state as non-empty.
low_band.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestB7GnowebWithNoRealmsIsNotEmpty -v ./... (from tests/b7-claims-cap-bounds_test.go)

low_band.summary: modFlags says it reads "the two booleans we care about"; nothing ever reads Pkg.Draft
low_band.failure_scenario: Pkg.Draft is parsed for every package on every run and consulted nowhere: `grep -rn "Draft" misc/gnopreview` returns only the field declaration at plan.go:58 and the assignment at plan.go:142. examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm is the one draft package in the walked tree, and it is previewed like any other. Either the field and half of modFlags are dead and go, or draft realms were meant to be filtered and are not.
low_band.verify_by: grep -rn "Draft" misc/gnopreview — expect a reader, observe only the declaration and the assignment
low_band.evidence: plan.go:58 (field), plan.go:142 (assignment) are the only hits; grep -rln '^[[:space:]]*draft[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*true' examples --include=gnomod.toml = examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm/gnomod.toml

low_band.summary: Realm is documented as "lives under gno.land/r/" but matches "/r/" anywhere in the path
low_band.failure_scenario: strings.Contains(rel, "/r/") over the repo-relative dir also matches a package under examples/gno.land/p/ whose own path carries an /r/ segment, which would be classified as a realm, entered into Realms, and crawled at gnoweb's realm URL. No such package exists today (find examples/gno.land -type d -path '*/r/*' ! -path 'examples/gno.land/r/*' returns 0), so this is latent: the first p/ package with an /r/ path segment breaks the classification silently.
